messages.content: When will be sunset in Beijing today?

function.name: calculate_sunrise
function.description: Calculate the time of sunrise for a specific date and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which sunrise time needs to be calculated.

date.description: The date for which sunrise time needs to be calculated in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not provided, current date is considered. Default: 1998-12-03

format.description: Format in which the time should be returned. If not provided, default format 'HH:MM' is considered.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have a function that directly gives me the sunset time. I can calculate sunrise times, but I can’t compute sunset times from the data I have. If you’d like, I can give you the sunrise time for Beijing today (or another date) instead.
message.reasoning: We need to call function calculate_sunrise but we want sunset. The function only calculates sunrise. There's no function for sunset. We can approximate by calling calculate_sunrise with location "Beijing" and date "today"? But we don't have today's date. We could use default date 1998-12-03. But that's wrong. We might need to compute sunset manually. But we can't. So we can respond that we cannot compute sunset. Or we can ask for clarification. Probably best to say we don't have function for sunset.
